subject: general
question: Which of the following is the correct representation of a number of atoms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**(given mass/molar mass) × Avogadro number**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Here's a breakdown of the formula:

__
 
• "given mass": This refers to the mass of the substance you are considering, typically given in grams.
 
• "molar mass": This represents the molar mass of the substance, which is the mass of one mole of that substance. It is expressed in grams per mole.
 
• "Avogadro's number": This constant is denoted by "Nₐ" or "L" and has a value of approximately 6.022 × 10²³. It represents the number of particles (atoms, molecules, ions) in one mole of a substance.
 
• The correct representation of the number of atoms is (given mass/molar mass) × Avogadro number.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The formula can be understood in the following steps:

 
• 
 
Divide the given mass of the substance (in grams) by the molar mass of the substance (in grams per mole). This gives you the number of moles of the substance.

 
 
• (given mass / molar mass)
 
 
 
• 
 
Multiply the number of moles by Avogadro's number to obtain the number of atoms.

 
 
• (given mass / molar mass) × Avogadro's number
 
 

18
